sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: BROAD UPR LOW WILL REMAIN QSTNRY OVER HUDSON BAY THROUGH THU WHILE SEVERAL LOW AMPLITUDE DISTURBANCES MOVE E ON ITS SRN PERIPHERY. UPR RIDGES WILL PERSIST OVER NM/TX AND WRN ATLANTIC. BETWEEN THE RIDGES...A SUBTROPICAL CIRCULATION WILL LINGER OVER MS. A BELT OF ENHANCED WLY FLOW EXTENDING FROM THE NRN GRT BASIN AND NRN RCKYS INTO THE NRN PLNS/UPR MS VLY WILL MARK THE NRN FRINGE OF THE NM/TX RIDGE. AT LWR LEVELS...MAIN FEATURE OF NOTE WILL BE FRONT NOW OVER THE NRN PLNS/UPR MS VLY. THE ERN PART OF THE BOUNDARY SHOULD PROGRESS SLOWLY SE INTO CNTRL WI/NRN MI BY 12Z THU...WHILE THE WRN PART REMAINS NEARLY STNRY FROM SD INTO MT.

sections.title: NRN PLNS/UPR MS VLY THIS AFTN/EVE
sections.text: AFOREMENTIONED FRONT SHOULD BE THE FOCUS FOR AFTN/EVE STORMS OVER THE NRN PLNS/UPR MS VLY THIS PERIOD AS BOUNDARY SETTLES SLOWLY SE AHEAD OF EXPANDING SFC ANTICYCLONE IN SK/AB. SATELLITE SUGGESTS PRESENCE OF AN IMPULSE IN BELT OF ENHANCED WNW FLOW OVER ERN MT/WY THAT SHOULD CONTINUE E INTO THE ERN DAKOTAS/WRN MN BY LATE TODAY. IN GENERAL...HOWEVER...UPR LVL FORCING FOR ASCENT OVER MOST OF THE SLIGHT RISK AREA WILL BE WEAK. NEVERTHELESS... COMBINATION OF SFC HEATING AND LOW LVL WAA/UPLIFT ALONG FRONT SHOULD FOSTER INCREASING STORM COVERAGE FROM NRN WI AND MN WSW INTO ERN SD AND POSSIBLY NEB LATER TODAY/EARLY TONIGHT. STRONGLY VEERED DEEP LAYER FLOW SHOULD SUPPORT SUSTAINED STORMS/SUPERCELLS...WITH DEEP WNWLY SHEAR RANGING FROM 40 TO 50 KTS. STORM COVERAGE SHOULD BECOME INCREASINGLY SPARSE WITH WWD EXTENT INTO SD. BUT THOSE THAT DO FORM THERE WILL HAVE ACCESS TO SUBSTANTIALLY MORE INSTABILITY COMPARED TO POINTS FARTHER EAST. COMBINATION OF DEEP EML AND AMPLE MOISTURE /PW AROUND 1 INCH/ COULD YIELD ONE OR TWO SUPERCELLS WITH VERY LARGE HAIL/DMGG WIND AND A COUPLE TORNADOES. A FEW STRONG TO SVR STORMS COULD PERSIST INTO LATE EVE IN ZONE OF LOW LVL WAA OVER ERN SD...NEB...NRN IA...AND S

sections.title: NRN UT INTO WRN WY THIA AFTN/EVE
sections.text: SHORTWAVE TROUGH IN BELT OF ENHANCED FLOW ON FRINGE OF NM/TX RIDGE WILL ALLOW DEEP TROPICAL MOISTURE TO SPREAD NEWD INTO UT/SWRN WY LATER TODAY. COMBINATION OF 25-30 KT DEEP UNIDIRECTIONAL SWLY FLOW WITH INCREASING MOISTURE AND SFC HEATING SHOULD SUPPORT ORGANIZATION OF STRONG DIURNAL STORMS INTO BANDS/CLUSTERS. SOME OF THESE MAY CONTAIN SMALL BOWING SEGMENTS WITH ISOLD DMGG WIND.

sections.title: LWR MS/TN VLYS THIS AFTN
sections.text: SUB-TROPICAL CIRCULATION EXPECTED TO REMAIN MORE OR LESS STNRY OVER MS THIS PERIOD...WITH PERHAPS A SLIGHT NNEWD DRIFT. DAYTIME HEATING SHOULD SUPPORT SCTD TSTMS IN VERY MOIST /PW AROUND 2.50 INCHES/ ERN AND NERN QUADRANTS OF SYSTEM. CURRENT VWP DATA...AND SOME MODEL FORECASTS...SUGGEST THAT LOW LVL VEERING PROFILES MAY BE SUFFICIENT TO SUPPORT LOW LVL STORM ROTATION IN ANY SUSTAINED UPDRAFTS. THUS...ADDITIONAL A LOW CONDITIONAL RISK FOR TORNADOES OVER PARTS OF MS...AL...AND TN THROUGH EARLY EVE. ..CORFIDI/HURLBUT.. 08/18/2010

sections.title: NRN PLAINS INTO UPPER GREAT LAKES
sections.text: INTENSIFICATION OF LARGE-SCALE TROUGH OVER ONTARIO INTO THE GREAT LAKES IS FORECAST THIS PERIOD WITH UPSTREAM HEIGHTS GRADUALLY BUILDING OVER THE NRN HIGH PLAINS IN ADVANCE OF NEXT SYSTEM AMPLIFYING OVER THE NRN INTERMOUNTAIN REGION INTO GREAT BASIN. WITHIN THIS BROADER FLOW REGIME...MORNING WATER VAPOR IMAGERY HINTS AT A LOW-AMPLITUDE IMPULSE/JET STREAK OVER ND WHICH WILL TRANSLATE RAPIDLY SEWD THROUGH MN INTO WI TODAY. AT THE SURFACE...A BAROCLINIC ZONE EXISTS FROM LK SUPERIOR WSWWD TO LOW PRESSURE OVER CNTRL SD AND THEN WNWWD ACROSS SRN MT. THE ERN EXTENSION OF THIS BOUNDARY WILL CONTINUE TO PUSH EWD/ESEWD THROUGH THE UPPER GREAT LAKES WHILE WRN PART OF BOUNDARY BECOMES QUASI-STATIONARY OR RETREATS SLOWLY NWD. ELEVATED TSTMS ARE GRADUALLY INTENSIFYING ALONG/N OF SURFACE FRONT OVER THE RED RIVER VALLEY THIS MORNING...SUPPORTED BY MODERATE ELEVATED INSTABILITY /REF. 12Z ABR SOUNDING/ AND INCREASED FORCING ATTENDANT TO MIDLEVEL SYSTEM MENTIONED ABOVE. CURRENT VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY INDICATES THE PRESENCE OF WIDESPREAD LOW CLOUDS WITHIN PRE-FRONTAL WARM SECTOR FROM ERN SD EWD INTO NRN WI. WHILE INITIAL DESTABILIZATION WILL BE SLOWED BY THESE CLOUDS...DEEPER PBL MIXING SHOULD ALLO

sections.title: PARTS OF MS/AL INTO TN/VA/NC
sections.text: GLANCING INFLUENCE OF MIDLEVEL TROUGH PROGRESSING EWD THROUGH THE OH VALLEY INTO MID ATLANTIC STATES SHOULD MAINTAIN AN ACTIVE CORRIDOR OF TSTM CLUSTERS ALONG ERN/SRN PERIPHERY OF MORE DENSE CLOUD COVER. HERE...THE COMBINATION OF A VERY MOIST AIR MASS /I.E. PW VALUES OF 2.0-2.8 INCHES/ AND DAYTIME HEATING WILL YIELD A MODERATELY UNSTABLE AIR MASS WITH MLCAPE VALUES APPROACHING 1000-2000 J/KG. CURRENT PLAN VIEW VWP DATA INDICATE A BELT OF 30-40 KT WSWLY MIDLEVEL FLOW FROM TN INTO THE MID ATLANTIC STATES WHICH MAY ALLOW FOR THE ORGANIZATION OF A FEW STORM CLUSTERS WITH THE THREAT FOR LOCALLY STRONG WIND GUSTS.

sections.title: MT
sections.text: LARGE-SCALE FORCING WILL INCREASE TODAY IN ADVANCE OF MIDLEVEL SYSTEM WHICH WILL GRADUALLY DEAMPLIFY WHILE MOVING INTO MEAN RIDGE IN PLACE OVER THE NRN HIGH PLAINS. TERRAIN INFLUENCES AND THE PRESENCE OF A SURFACE BOUNDARY ACROSS THE SRN PART OF THE STATE WILL SERVE AS FOCI FOR ISOLATED TO WIDELY SCATTERED STORM FORMATION. GIVEN THE STEEP LAPSE RATES AND MODERATELY STRONG DEEP WNWLY SHEAR IN PLACE...SETUP WILL FAVOR LONGER-LIVED/ROTATING STORMS WITH A THREAT FOR SOME HAIL AND LOCALLY STRONG WIND GUSTS. ..MEAD/SMITH.. 08/18/2010

sections.title: NORTHERN PLAINS TO UPPER GREAT LAKES
sections.text: WHILE THE BOUNDARY LAYER HAS BEEN SLOW TO DESTABILIZE OWING TO CLOUD COVER/MODEST MOISTURE...EARLY DAY ELEVATED TSTMS CURRENTLY ONGOING FROM EASTERN MN INTO NORTHERN WI ARE EXPECTED TO GRADUALLY BECOME SURFACE BASED BY LATE AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING. DAMAGING WINDS ALONG WITH SEVERE HAIL WILL BECOME INCREASINGLY POSSIBLE. REFERENCE MESOSCALE DISCUSSION 1715 FOR ADDITIONAL DETAILS. FARTHER WEST...GIVEN NEUTRAL TO SLIGHTLY RISING UPPER HEIGHTS AND MORE MODEST MASS CONVERGENCE...THE SEVERE STORM THREAT IS STILL EXPECTED TO TREND MORE ISOLATED/CONDITIONAL WITH WESTWARD EXTENT ALONG THE SD FRONTAL ZONE/ADJACENT NORTHERN NEB. NONETHELESS...AMPLE DESTABILIZATION AND STRONG/VEERED WIND PROFILES...AIDED BY A STRENGTHENING LOW LEVEL JET THROUGH EARLY/MID EVENING...WILL SUPPORT AT LEAST AN ISOLATED RISK OF SUPERCELLS/BOW DEVELOPMENT WITH SEVERE HAIL/WINDS AND PERHAPS A TORNADO ALL POSSIBLE.

sections.title: ELSEWHERE
sections.text: WITH FEW CHANGES IN FORECAST REASONING BASED ON OBSERVATIONAL/SHORT TERM GUIDANCE TRENDS...PLEASE CONSULT PRIOR DISCUSSION BELOW. ..GUYER.. 08/18/2010 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1117 AM CDT WED AUG 18 2010/
